reviews.title: Bad airline service
reviews.text: Apparently rescheduling is now available via their app however found no such option. Upon connecting with the multiple times on different number finally someone helped to manual reschedule it. The reschedule payment link dint work after multiple retries. Finally I requested a refund on my non refundable flight and had to point out the fact that I have been trying for more than 3 hours at which point they finally agreed to reschedule it for me. reviews.title: Good flights between Kathmandu and Pokhara
reviews.text: The road from Kathmandu to Pokhara is often blocked by landslides and rockfalls during the monsoon season and in 2022 has been blocked several times. The quickest way to get to Pokhara is a 23 minute flight – much better than the 7 or 8 hour drive. All airlines in Nepal charge foreigners a higher fare than the locals and even if you are the only foreigner on a plane, you are paying over US$20 extra than all those sitting around you. Buddha Air is the biggest domestic service and I found them to be very well organised and both flights were good. Basically you take off, climb for about 5 minutes, level out for 5 minutes then descend and land. Buddha Air has built a new domestic terminal at Kathmandu airport which is clean with plenty of seating. You are then taken on a bus out to the plane and off you go. The plane was clean – an ATR72 twin engine turboprop short haul plane developed and produce in France and Italy which can carry between 72 and 78 passengers. Pokhara is a delight to land at – clean, spacious, surrounded by huge mountains with the beautiful Phewa Tal Lake in the centre, but very humid and hot during the monsoon. Can highly recommend Buddha Air – they seem to be well organised and both flights were good.

The domestic airport in Kathmandu is horrendous and combined with no or poor communication makes for misery. The voice communication is terrible and the screens have no or wrong information. reviews.title: Mountain Flight aka Everest Experience
reviews.text: Booked direct online to do the scenic flight passing the Himalayas and Mount Everest. About 8 Buddha Air flights were all scheduled at the exact same time (6:30am) so don’t expect to depart on time. Nor should your flight number be an indication of in which order you will depart. I was flight 101. The other flights were 100, 102, 103, 104, 200, 400, 600. Flight 103 went first. Then 400. There was no logic. I didn’t care, it’s Nepal, they do things their way! The main thing was we eventually left and had perfect skies and a great co pilot who took photos for us. We had seatbelts. Seats about 18 passengers. The small plane had only window seats someberyone gets a view. Windows oval shaped and row 7 has the wing obstructing view a little. Some little scratches,on the window as you would expect for old planes. Some condensation gathers as it goes up into the cold atmosphere. Pilot’s window provide great photos. Left side see the mountains first. We could visit the front to look out the clear cockpit windows lots of times. The weather was hazy on the ground (extreme pollution) but above the brown layer it was a perfect layer. You get a little mountain map and a certificate at the end. Well worth the money. Highly recommend it. (Did not fly to Pokhara, just had to enter a destination to submit this review)
